# Service Provider Interface

A simple example that demonstrates the Service Provider Interface in conjunction
with the Java Module System. The example makes used of an in-memory database to
demonstrates a realistic use case.

---

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

## Run the example

1. Build the application

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean package
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the JAR files were created and copied to the
   `./target/libs` and `./target/libs-spring` directory.

   ```shell
   tree --dirsfirst --sort=name --prune -P '*.jar' './target'
   ```

   The application JAR files

3. Describe the JAR files

   Describe the `app.jar`

   ```shell
   jar --describe-module --file './target/libs/app.jar'
   ```

   The application module description

   ```
   demo.app@1.0.0 jar:file:///home/opc/workspace/workshop-java-module-system/examples/service-provider-interfaces/./target/libs/app.jar!/module-info.class
   requires demo.sl
   requires java.base mandated
   contains demo.app
   main-class demo.app.Main
   ```

   ```shell
   jar --describe-module --file './target/libs-spring/app-spring.jar'
   ```

   ```
   demo.spring@1.0.0 jar:file:///home/opc/workspace/workshop-java-module-system/examples/service-provider-interfaces/./target/libs-spring/app-spring.jar!/module-info.class
   requires demo.spi
   requires java.base mandated
   ```

4. Run the application

   Run the plain application (not the Spring boot version)

   ```shell
   java \
     --module-path './target/libs' \
     --add-modules ALL-MODULE-PATH \
     --module demo.app
   ```

   This will produce a random quote, one from each service provider.

   ```
   When the going gets tough, the tough get going. by Joe Kennedy (Service: demo.db.DbQuoteService)
   Get busy living or get busy dying. by Stephen King (Service: demo.mem.InMemoryQuoteService)
   ```

   Run the Spring application

   ```shell
   java \
     --module-path './target/libs-spring' \
     --add-modules ALL-MODULE-PATH \
     --module demo.spring
   ```

   This will produce a random quote, one from each service provider.

   ```
      ___                    ___________ _____           _____            _              ______                                           _
   ```
